newsitem.title: UK: From the Flightdeck - The Air Cargo Week in Review.
newsitem.headline: From the Flightdeck - The Air Cargo Week in Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the global air cargo industry in the week September 23 - September 27.
*SEPTEMBER 23**
KUALA LUMPUR - The Business Times says Malaysia's second national airline, Pacific Eagle, will begin scheduled flights on November 17.
SYDNEY - Australia's Federal Aviation Corp says it has approved A$56 million for road development work at Sydney airport.
BANGKOK - An airline official says a Thai Airways airbus with 160 people on board was forced to make an emergency landing after a fire warning signal was triggered.
GENEVA - Geneva's statistical office Cointrin airport saw a drop in freight and passenger traffic in July.

FRANKFURT - The air noise commission, which represents local authorities close to the airport says local authorities in the Frankfurt region have warned a 50 percent cut in night landing fees for freighters at Frankfurt airport will generate additional noise for residents.
MOSCOW - Russian private cargo airlines Volga-Dnepr spokesman says it had sales of $63.5 million during the first eight months of this year compared with $42.3 million in the same period 1995.

ZURICH - FIATA (International Federation of Freight Forwarders Accusations) says a meeting of the affiliated the Airfreight Institute (AFI), forms part of the programme for it annual congress, to be held in Caracus, between September 29 and October 3.
AMSTERDAM - Cargonaut, the electronic messaging system for the Dutch airfreight industry says it recorded significantly more use last year than in previous years.
WARSAW - Poland's national carrier LOT says cargo traffic increased by 16.8 percent to 10,050 tonnes in the first eight months of this year from the same period 1995.
MOSCOW - Aeroflot company spokeswoman says it will begin a regular service between Moscow and Cancun, Mexico from October 26.
WARSAW - DHL says it and LOT have launched a joint cargo connection between Warsaw and Brussels via Germany.
PARIS - Aeroports de Paris(ADP) says New York was the top originating gateway for import traffic into Charles de Gualle and Orly airports last month despite a decline in tonnage.
* ADP says New York was the top destination from Charles de Gualle and Orly airports.
* ADP says New York was the top airport gateway for imports to Charles de Gaulle and Orly airport in the first eight months of 1996. It was also the top export destination.
HONG KONG - SAS says its "pioneering" use of a barge to transfer air cargo from Hong Kong to Macau airport over the past six months has been a surprising success.
FRANKFURT - Flughafen airport said its subsidiary Ineuropa handling will start handling operations at four Spanish airports in competition to Iberia from November 4.
LONDON - Martinair senior vice president Meta Ullings says it is planning to announce an increase in rates on the freighter flights it operates to Taiwan and Hong Kong.

PARIS - ADP figures show the percentage of global air cargo traffic handled at the Paris airports in the first eight months of 1996 arriving and departing on full-freighter flights was up 0.5 percent on the same period last year at 39.3 percent.
FRANKFURT - Germany holiday airline LTU International Airways says it will hold electronic ticket auctions on the Compuserve online service.
* LTU says it will start services to Phoenix, Arizona and Chiang Mai in Thailand from November 4.
HONG KONG - China Airlines and Cathay Pacific says two months after EVA Air entered the busy Hong Kong-Taipei sector, there has been no significant impact on cargo volumes.
BONN - A government ministry says a work group of government officials and businessmen is studying how majority control of Lufthansa can remain in German hands after full privatisation.
MILOCER, Montenegro - A senior government official says Montenegro is considering buying three aircraft in a bid to boost its tourism industry.

WASHINGTON - The U.S. General Services Administration says it has awarded contracts to 18 airlines for discount rates on more than 6,100 domestic and international routes for federal travellers that are expected to save $2.4 billion during the upcoming fiscal year.
MIAMI - Greenwich Air Services says USAir Group has decided not to renew its five-year contract for CFM56-3 engines with them.
FORT WORTH - American Airlines says that William Boesch had retired from his post as president of the airline's cargo division, which he had held for the last eight years.
ROME - Alitalia says it has signed a deal with Singapore Airlines to develop a modern cargo management system.
NEWARK - Kiwi International Airlines says its August load factor increased to 62 percent from 54 percent a year ago period.
ORLANDO - AirWays Corp says that its second quarter loss for the period ending September 30 may range between $0.40 and $0.45 a share, which is below analysts' expectations.
**SEPTEMBER 24**
JAKARTA - Indonesia says it has launched efforts to develop Batam, an island near Singapore, into a cargo hub with a request to Lufthansa to run services to the island.
BRUSSELS - DHL Aviation says it added two Boeing 727Fs to its intra-European fleet earlier this month.
ST. PETERSBURG - SAS company official says it has started regular passenger flights between Stockholm and the northern Russian City of Arkhangelsk.

MAASTRICHT - BA World Cargo business manager Western Europe, Henk van Ameijde, says it is setting up its former trucking hub at Maastricht-Aachen airport in the southern Netherlands as an administration headquarters for its Western European airfreight operations.
AMSTERDAM - Dutch transport group Racon director Leen Lok says Racon and airport operating company Rotterdam Airport BV has opened a new airfreight handling facility at Rotterdam airport.
PARIS - ADP figures show January-August 1996 postal traffic handled at the Paris airport, Charles de Gaulle and Orly totalled 84,394 tonnes, an increase of 4.1 percent on the same period last year.
* ADP figures show Schipol airport recorded the highest percentage gain in cargo traffic last month among the EU's top cargo-handling airports.

MANILA - Bank of Philippine Islands says it will not subscribe to the capital increase for Philippine Airlines, effectively clearing the way for controversial tycoon Lucio Tan to extend his control of the troubled national carrier.
ISTANBUL - Turkish Airlines says it will launch a twice a week flights between Istanbul and Sarajevo with a stopover in Zagreb.
FRANKFURT - Delta Airlines regional director cargo sales and services Europe, Danita Waterfall says it aims to improve ex-Europe cargo revenues by 15 percent in the 1996-97 fiscal year.
* Waterfall added it is discussing operating a joint Europe-U.S. freighter service with partner airlines Swissair and Sabena.
* Delta says it has appointed new cargo general sales agents for the Netherlands and Belgium as part of a Europe sales re-structuring.
* Waterfall says it will drop one of its two daily passenger Frankfurt-New York flights from November 1.
* Waterfall says a cargo sales agreement for Russia with Chapman Freeborn Airmarketing has been held up by red tape.
HONG KONG - United Airlines says it will restart its non-stop flight Hong Kong and Chicago in 1997 after a better than anticipated first season.
* United Airlines senior vice-president international Chris Bowers says work is under way to convert the first two aircraft for Uniteds new all-cargo service to Asia.

ROTTERDAM - Transport and storage group Hes Beheer says it planned to shed 280 jobs at its European Bulk Services unit to safeguard EBS's future in the face of a structual decline in bulk cargo volumes.

PARIS - ADP figures show Air France increased its share of global air cargo tonnage handled at the two Paris airports, Charles de Gualle and Orly, in the first eight months of 1996, compared to 1995 as a whole.
BOMBAY - A spokesman says a committee appointed by Air-India submitted its preliminary report on purchase of aircraft valued at over $2.0 billion planned by the national carrier.
SOFIA - Bulgaria's police says it would strengthen security precautions around the Sofia airport following recent bomb threats.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong's financial secretary Donald Tsang says economic growth in the Asia-Pacific would fuel global aviation traffic in coming years.
MADRID - Industry minister Josep Pigue says Spain expects airline Iberia to form an alliance with a foreign company by the end of the year.
